prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance to the right front corner, draws uke in firmly, and: pivoting on the left foot: sweeps up the outside of uke's right leg from the front with the right leg, throwing uke forward.

Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall) From kumi-kata, tori turns in with mae-mawari-sabaki, sweeps uke's right leg and throws uke forward; uke lands taking ukemi. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement) to break uke's balance forward, sweeps uke's right leg with the right leg, and throws uke forward. Cooperation of uke: So that tori does not bend forward, uke is thrown while arching the upper body moderately. How to take the ukemi: In time with tori's harai-goshi, uke takes mae-mawari-ukemi (forward rolling breakfall).

Tori sweeps lightly with the right leg and throws uke forward. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement), sweeps uke lightly with the right leg, and throws uke forward. How to take the ukemi: Uke rotates sideways about the right foot and takes yoko-ukemi (side breakfall).

Tori pushes uke; as uke pushes back, tori turns in with ushiro-mawari-sabaki and applies the technique. Push uke, and at the moment uke pushes back, apply the technique with ushiro-mawari-sabaki (backward turning body movement).

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori's tsurite (lifting hand) is stretched out, so the kuzushi (breaking of balance) is not working.
Do not apply the technique bent forward, in a posture that drives the head into the mat.
